name: stuck-pagination
description:
A Kandji that stops advancing and answers every offset with the same page. The walk's only exit is a page that comes back empty, so this shape produces no exit at all: it used to fetch the same page until the task timed out, with nothing in the log to say why.

The no-progress check is the working guard -- the CONFIG maxPages ceiling behind it (enforced by pager()) is ten million records deep and exists only so an adversarially rotating server still terminates, by raising rather than truncating silently. A page whose row ids are identical to the previous page's means the server ignored `offset` or replayed a cached response, and the walk stops on the first repeat and says so, which is what log_contains pins.

The first page carries a real device, so the run still proves rows are parsed, detailed, and reported. The second page carries one row with no device_id -- different content, so the walk correctly continues -- and the third repeats it, which is the first genuine repeat and the stop. Rows are single because page fullness is irrelevant to this walk: it continues on ANY non-empty page.

The route matching offset=900 exists ONLY as a terminator for a regression. Serving the stuck page with when_exhausted=repeat_last alone would make an unguarded walk run to a 33,334-page ceiling and fail this scenario by timing out rather than by failing an assertion; with the terminator, an unguarded walk stops one request later and fails on request_count, requests_absent and the missing log line instead.

namespaced_ids is skipped for the reason recorded in happy: the id is the bare Kandji device id with no tenant scope.

log_contains: kandji: pagination stopped making progress at offset 600; the server repeated the previous page. Retrieved 1 assets; the API does not report a total
